data.name: Eber
data.long_meaning: In the Old Testament, Eber is a descendant of Shem, the son of Noah. This name is derived from the Hebrew word ‘avar’, meaning ‘stranger’ or ‘foreigner’. Eber is the father of two notable figures in the Bible: Peleg and Joktan.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of our spiritual origins, rooted in the divine.

in_english.name: Eber
in_english.long_meaning: a Hebrew name derived from the root עבר, referring to one of the sons of Shem, and meaning beyond the river or crossing, with spiritual and cultural significance in Christian tradition

biblical_reference.note: Eber is mentioned as the father of Peleg and an ancestor of Abraham

data.cultural_impact: The name Eber carries a significant cultural impact due to its biblical origins. As a descendant of Shem, Eber is part of the lineage of the ancient Hebrews, an important branch of human history. Furthermore, the name’s association with the concept of being a ‘stranger’ or ‘foreigner’ speaks to themes of migration and exploration, which continue to resonate in today's globalized world.
data.spiritual_significance: Eber's name has a rich spiritual significance as it comes from the Hebrew root word 'avar', meaning 'other'. This implies a connection to the idea of God's infinite nature and the intricacies of His plan for humanity. Being a ‘stranger’ or ‘foreigner’ in this context refers to the spiritual journey of every human being, as we are all travelers on the path of life, seeking to understand our purpose and connection to a higher power. Additionally, Eber's association with his offspring Peleg, who is said to have lived during a time of intense turmoil and division, emphasizes the importance of maintaining faith and unity in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Genesis 2:21 The name Eber carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Eber is the name of the first man God created from Adam's rib. He is the progenitor of the human race.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Joshua 10:24-25 The name Eber carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: After Joshua's victory over the Amorites, the land was apportioned among the tribes. One of the cities given to the Kenite tribe was called Hebron, which was formerly called Kirjath-arba (City of Four), and the Canaanite who owned it before was called Sheshai, son of Ahiman. After Sheshai's death, his city was ruled by a certain Eber, a descendant of Sheshai.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Eber is derived from the Hebrew language and means 'ever.' In the Bible, Eber is the name of a descendant of Shem, one of Noah's three sons. In modern times, the name Eber is seen as a unique and meaningful choice for both boys and girls. It is often used in the context of ancestry research and exploration of Biblical names. Eber is a popular choice on baby-naming websites such as BabyCenter and Nameberry. Ancestry.com, a leading genealogy website, also lists Eber as a historical name of interest for those researching their family history.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Eber, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Eber meaning "My father is a stranger" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Eber signifies "my father is a stranger" in Hebrew, reflecting the inherent belief in God as our true Father, even when our earthly fathers may seem distant or unknown. It is a reminder of our spiritual roots and the promise of a loving relationship with the Divine.
